title: An ethical will
hook: a letter of values left for those who come after
tomorrow: Saba wants to talk about his funeral. at dinner. on purpose. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rabbi Akiva's visit and a swept floor: carers are holy. Today, someone recovering starts thinking about what he'll leave behind, and it isn't furniture.

A voice memo on a phone: a grandmother singing happy birthday, slightly off key, and nobody can bring themselves to delete it. Sometimes what we keep isn't the stuff at all. It's a voice, a sentence, a way of doing things. So what goes in a letter written for after you're gone? Jewish tradition has a name for that letter, and the Torah sketches one.
screen: `A VOICE MEMO NOBODY DELETES.` → `NOT THE STUFF.` → `A LETTER FOR AFTER.`

segments.voice: The name is tzava'ah, an ethical will. Not who gets the house. What you hope they'll keep. The sketch is in Genesis, where God says of Abraham, in the JPS translation, "that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice." A legacy of the way, not the wealth. Jacob gathers his sons before he dies and speaks to each one. King David, near his end, tells Solomon: be strong, and show yourself a man. And the custom grew. A medieval father, Judah ibn Tibbon, wrote his son a long letter that tradition still remembers, telling him to make his books his companions and his bookshelves his gardens. An ethical will can be a page or three lines. What I learned. What I hope you keep. What I'm grateful for, or sorry for. People write them at eighty and at thirty, healthy or sick. It isn't a goodbye. It's a way of saying, while you still can, the thing your family would otherwise have to guess. Something to tell a friend tonight: one Jewish father's letter to his son asked him to treat his bookshelves like gardens.
screen: `TZAVA'AH: NOT THE HOUSE. THE WAY.` · `ABRAHAM, JACOB, DAVID.` · `BOOKSHELVES LIKE GARDENS.` · `WHAT THEY'D OTHERWISE GUESS.` · then, large: `LEAVE YOUR VALUES.`

segments.voice: By hand, write three lines to someone who will come after you. One: something you learned the hard way. Two: something you hope they'll keep. Three: something you're grateful for. Fold the paper and put it somewhere safe.
screen: `ONE: SOMETHING YOU LEARNED.` · `TWO: SOMETHING TO KEEP.` · `THREE: SOMETHING YOU'RE GRATEFUL FOR.`

segments.voice: Tzava'ah: an ethical will. A letter of values for the people who come after, in the line of Abraham, Jacob and David.
Keep this one: leave your values, because your family shouldn't have to guess them. Talk soon.

howItsDone: Some Jews write an ethical will (tzava'ah) to leave values, hopes and blessings to their families, alongside or apart from a legal will, and some read one aloud to family while they are alive.

chat.meaning: A tzava'ah passes on what you hope your family keeps, in the line of Abraham, Jacob and David. Writing one isn't morbid; it saves them guessing.
